en: The *Buddha-spoken Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Delivering the Hungry Ghosts with Flaming Mouths*.
By the Duke of Su, Grand Master of State Ceremonial, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
with an appanage of three thousand households, recipient of the purple robe, posthumously titled Minister of Works and conferred the posthumous name Dajian (Great Mirror).

Translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Monastery, who possesses Great and Vast Wisdom, under imperial decree. At that time, the World-Honored One was at the Nyagrodha Monastery in the city of Kapilavastu, surrounded before and behind by a vast assembly of bhikṣus and bodhisattvas, expounding the Dharma for them.
At that time, Ānanda was dwelling alone in a quiet place, reflecting upon the teachings he had received.

Then, after the third watch of the night had passed, he saw a hungry ghost named "Flaming Mouth" (Yamukha). Its form was hideous; its body was withered and emaciated, fire blazed from its mouth, its throat was as narrow as the point of a needle, its hair was disheveled, and its claws and fangs were long and sharp. It was most terrifying. Standing before Ānanda, it addressed him, saying:
"In three days' time, your life will come to an end, and you shall immediately be reborn among the hungry ghosts."
At that time, having heard these words, Ānanda was struck with fear and anxiety; he asked the hungry ghost:
"If, after my death, I am reborn as a hungry ghost, what skillful means should I practice to escape this suffering?"
At that time, the hungry ghost said to Ānanda:

"If tomorrow you can bestow alms upon a hundred thousand nayutas of hungry ghosts as numerous as the sands of the Ganges River, as well as a hundred thousand brahmin seers and others, giving each one measure of food and drink using the *droṇa* used in the kingdom of Magadha, and furthermore make offerings to the Triple Gem on my behalf, you shall increase your lifespan, and I shall be freed from the suffering of the hungry ghosts and attain rebirth in the heavens."

When Ānanda saw these *yānmouth* hungry ghosts—whose bodies were emaciated, withered, and extremely hideous; whose mouths blazed with fire, whose throats were like the point of a needle, whose hair was disheveled, and whose body hair and claws were long and sharp—and heard such discordant words, he was struck with great terror, and the hairs on his body all stood on end.

He immediately rose from his seat, hastened to where the Buddha was, prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, and with his body trembling, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“May you save me from my suffering!”
Why is this? While I was dwelling in a secluded place, recollecting the Dharma I had been taught, I saw a *yāma-mukha* hungry ghost who spoke to me, saying:
"In three days' time, your life will surely come to an end, and you will be reborn among the hungry ghosts."
I immediately asked:
"How may I be delivered from this suffering?
The hungry ghost replied:

"If you can now bestow various kinds of food and drink upon hundreds of thousands of nayutas of *gangesālukā* *preta*s, as well as upon hundreds of thousands of Brahmins and sages, your lifespan will be increased."
"World-Honored One!
How can I now prepare food for so many hungry ghosts, sages, and others?
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Do not fear now!

I have a skillful means by which you shall be able to provide various kinds of food and drink for hundreds of thousands of *gatis* of hungry ghosts, as well as for the various Brahmins and ṛṣis; do not give rise to grief or distress."
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"There is a dhāraṇī called 'Infinite Majestic Virtue, Sovereign Radiance, and Supreme Wondrous Power.

If there are those who recite this dhāraṇī, they will be able to provide sufficient, exquisite food and drink for as many hungry ghosts, brahmin seers, and others as there are grains of sand in hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Ganges Rivers."
Each and every one of this multitude, even down to the individual, shall receive seventy-seven *droṇas* of food using the measures employed in the kingdom of Magadha. Ānanda!

Because I, in a previous life as a brahmin, received this dhāraṇī from the presence of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and the Tathāgata Lokeśvararāja, I was able to distribute various kinds of food and drink to immeasurable hungry ghosts and various sages, causing those hungry ghosts to be liberated from their bodies of suffering and attain rebirth in the heavens.
"Ānanda! If you now receive and uphold this, your merit and lifespan will both increase.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this dhāraṇī for Ānanda:
"Namo sarva-tathāgatāvalokite oṃ saṃbhara saṃbhara hūṃ. The Buddha told Ānanda:

"If there are sons or daughters of good family who desire long life, increasing merit, and prosperity, and wish to quickly fulfill the dāna-pāramitā without any obstacles at all times, including every morning, they should take a clean vessel, fill it with pure water, place a small amount of cooked rice, parched grain flour, various cakes, and other foods therein, and rest their right hand upon the vessel. They should recite the preceding dhāraṇī seven times, and then invoke the names of the four Tathāgatas:"

*Namo bhagavate prajñāpāramitā-tathāgatāya*. (This means: Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna. By the power of reciting the name of the Tathāgata Prabhūtaratna, one is able to destroy all the evil karma of stinginess accumulated over many lifetimes by various spirits, and immediately attains the perfection of merit and virtue.

*Namo bhagavate surūpāya tathāgatāya*. (This means: "Homage to the Tathāgata of Wondrous Physical Form. By the power of reciting the name of the Tathāgata Surūpa, one can destroy the ugly and evil forms of all ghosts and immediately attain a body endowed with perfect physical marks.

*Namo bhagavate vipula-garbhodgata-tāyine tathāgatāya*. (In Chinese: 廣博身如來). By the power of reciting the name of the Tathāgata Vipula-garbhodgata, the throats of all hungry ghosts are made wide and spacious, so that the food offered may satisfy them to their heart's content.

*Namo bhagavate apāyagaṇāya tathāgatāya.* (This means "Homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata who has transcended the hosts of miserable states. By the power of reciting the name of the Tathāgata Apāyagaṇa, all the terrors of the various hungry ghosts shall be completely extinguished, and they shall be liberated from the realm of hungry ghosts.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"If noble sons or daughters of good family, having already invoked the empowerment by reciting the names of the four Tathāgatas, snap their fingers seven times, take a food vessel, and pour its contents over clean ground with arms outstretched."

Having made this offering, there appeared before him from the four directions hundreds of thousands of nayutas of hungry ghosts, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, each with seventy-seven *dronas* of food from the kingdom of Magadha.
Having received this food, they were all fully satisfied; these various hungry ghosts all cast off their ghostly bodies and were reborn in the heavens. "Ānanda!

If there are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās who constantly empower food with this secret mantra and the names of the four Tathāgatas before giving it to the ghosts, they will be able to fulfill immeasurable merit and virtue. This is equal to the merit of making offerings to hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Tathāgatas, without any difference. Their lifespan will be extended, their physical strength and vitality will increase, and their roots of goodness will be complete. No non-humans, yakṣas, rākṣasas, or other malevolent spirits and ghosts will dare to harm them, and they will further accomplish immeasurable merit, virtue, and longevity."

"If one wishes to give to various brāhmaṇas, ṛṣis, and others, one should fill a vessel with pure food and drink, empower it twenty-one times with the aforementioned secret mantra, and cast it into a stream of pure flowing water."
Having done so, he immediately made offerings of exquisite food fit for celestial seers to hundreds of thousands of koṭis of Brahmin seers, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.

Because those rishis had obtained the consecrated food (*adhiṣṭhita-bhakṣa*), through the majestic power of their secret mantras (*mantra*), each accomplished their fundamental aspirations and various virtuous merits. Simultaneously, they each made this vow:
"May these people who eat this food have long lives, physical strength, and peace;
furthermore, may whatever they see or hear be understood with correct and pure comprehension, and may they fully accomplish the majestic power of Brahmā and practice the conduct of Brahmā."

"Furthermore, one will possess merit equal to that of making offerings to as many Tathāgatas as there are grains of sand in a hundred thousand Ganges Rivers, such that no enemies or adversaries can cause them harm.

"If bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās wish to make offerings to the Triple Gem—the Buddha, the Dharma, and the Saṃgha—they should use incense, flowers, and pure food, empower these with the aforementioned secret mantra twenty-one times, and present them to the Triple Gem."

These good sons and good daughters shall thereby accomplish the offering of celestial delicacies of supreme flavor to the Triple Gem—the Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha—filling the worlds of the ten directions; they shall also perform the merits of praising, entreating, and rejoicing [in others' merit], and will be constantly remembered and praised by all Buddhas, with heavenly deities and benevolent spirits always coming to protect them, thereby fulfilling the *dānapāramitā*.
“Ānanda! Follow my words, practice according to the Dharma, and widely proclaim and disseminate it, so that all sentient beings may universally see and hear it, thereby attaining immeasurable merit.”
"This is called the *Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Saving the Hungry Ghosts with Flaming Mouths and Suffering Sentient Beings*; you should uphold it by this name.
When the entire great assembly, including Ānanda and the others, had heard what the Buddha said, they received it with single-minded faith and joyfully put it into practice.
The Dhāraṇī Sūtra for Delivering the Hungry Ghosts with Flaming Mouths (Yamāntaka)
